document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Newly Published Documents Cast Doubt on Claims Taliban Will Give Up al Qaeda | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret] OSINT summary previously published in the Archive's 'Haqqani History' posting. It calls the strategy of separating the Taliban from al Qaeda 'farfetched' since low-level fighters are used by both. It says al Qaeda plays a coordinating and strategic role among allied groups, supporting the Taliban's aim of forcing Western forces out and regaining control of the government.

events.description: Mullah Omar issued a statement seeking legitimate relations with all countries and expressing solidarity with Iran; Al Qaeda websites denounced the 'nationalist trend'.
First set of talks in Mecca under auspices of the Saudi king between Afghan officials and former Taliban figures, backed by the US.
Hekmatyar sent a letter to Karzai in the spring; a similar message in October.
Coalition operation at a home in Kundi village, Khost, targeting an al-Qa'ida-affiliated person; two men and a woman killed, six detained per coalition.
Kabul police shut down ERD Security Company and collected its weapons.
Mullah Omar issued a statement seeking legitimate relations with all countries and expressing solidarity with Iran.
A forged letter signed in the name of Jalaluddin Haqqani denounced Mullah Omar, probably a psychological operation.
First set of Mecca talks between Afghan officials and former Taliban figures under the auspices of the Saudi king.
In the spring Hekmatyar sent a letter to Karzai, with a similar message sent in October.
Foreign forces raided a home in Kundi village north of Khost city, killing two men and a woman, wounding another woman and detaining several people; Al-Qa'ida affiliation was alleged.
Acting Khost governor Sabari confirmed the raid and complained that foreign forces never inform Afghan authorities of such operations in advance.
Afghan Islamic Press published its report on the Khost raid, quoting Maj Patrick Sieber.
Hekmatyar sent a letter to Karzai in spring saying he was old and implying foreign troops should leave urban centers.
A similar message was sent from Hekmatyar to Karzai in October.
Kabul police shut down ERD Security Company and seized its weapons (Kalashnikovs, 18 PK machine-guns, six pistols).
Coalition forces raided a home in Kundi village north of Khost city; two men and a woman killed, another woman wounded, several detained.

key_claims: Afghan government and allies seek to split reconciled 'moderate' insurgents from hard-liners and separate the Taliban from Al Qaeda.
Jalaluddin Haqqani's network is described as independent of Omar's Taliban and closely aligned with Al Qaeda.
A letter attributed to Haqqani denouncing Omar was suspected to be a psychological operation by Afghan government or allies.
US-backed talks in Mecca under the Saudi king involved mostly low-ranking former Taliban figures.
Analyst comment judges a Taliban–Al Qaeda split functionally unlikely since the groups share low-level fighters and any separation would be only propaganda.
Analyst claims Al Qaeda provides coordination and strategic role among several syndicate organizations.
